what_happened: Scene L9/S9: black double-basin sink with a pull-down gooseneck faucet. The sponge sat on the counter just left of the sink. The cast-iron pan (pan_7, flat handle with a hanging hole) lay on the counter far left, with its handle pointing toward the robot. Stage 0 (sponge first): the sponge was grasped at 123 near its edge and carried over the left basin. At 164-172 it slipped out of the fingers and fell ~20 cm into the basin (at target from 138, stage 0 at 201). The fingers then closed fully (width 0.003 at 176) and stayed closed (0.001) until 1436. Stage 1 (pan): with the gripper still closed, the arm stretched to the far left (240-320) over the handle end. From 430 to 793 it repeatedly pushed down on the handle tip with the closed fingertips: ten 'holds' with lift 0-2 cm, widths never above 0.021. It never opened to grasp. At ~860-900 the sweep rotated the pan on the counter, and the arm left. Stage 2 anyway: 1100-1440 it moved to the faucet, opened the fingers at 1436-1448, pressed the lever from above and turned the water on at 1516 (handle 0.50). The pan stayed on the counter 0.34 m from the basin, so stage 2 never held.
causal_chain: sponge slips out at ~170 and the fingers close on nothing (176) -> the gripper stays closed for 1260 steps -> 360 steps of pushing the pan handle with closed fingers (430-793), never a real grasp -> the pan is abandoned on the counter -> the policy turns the water on at 1516 without the pan -> success condition false
self_recovery: The fallen sponge happened to land in the basin. It made no recovery for the pan: it kept poking with closed fingers and then moved on to the faucet.
official_criterion_notes: Stage 2 shows fixtures done_intervals [[1516,1600]] (water on) while the stage never completes, correctly, because the pan is outside. The packet's 'holds' 430-793 are pushes by closed fingers, not grasps (width <= 0.021 throughout). The 6.283 sink values are the wrap artefact of a tiny negative joint angle.

packet_facts: sponge hold 123-170 drop 0.202; at target from 138
pan holds 430-793 (10 intervals) lift <= 0.021, dist ~0.28-0.34; end dist 0.335

uncertain_about: Why the policy kept the gripper closed after the sponge slipped. The pan handle end was at the far left, close to the arm's reach, but it was reached; with open fingers a grasp looked geometrically possible.
